description: Build and first-flight years are estimates. Probably served with 299 IIKShAP, then stored at Yevpatoria; displayed at the Mikhailovskaya Battery when it housed the Ukrainian Navy museum, and still there. Open-air equipment display of the Mikhailovskaya Battery museum on the Northern Side of Sevastopol. russianplanes.net monument and registry cards, checked September 2026. Site recorded with country Russia as the airplane.museum schema requires; Crimea and Sevastopol are internationally recognised as Ukrainian territory under Russian occupation since 2014.
